newsitem.title: USA: Chinese warships to visit United States.
newsitem.headline: Chinese warships to visit United States.

text.p: Three Chinese Navy ships will visit U.S. naval bases in Hawaii and California next month in another sign of improving relations between Washington and Beijing, the Pentagon said on Thursday.

Announcement of the visits by the destroyers Harbin and Zhuhai and the naval oiler Nancang, negotiated during a December visit to Washington by Chinese Defense Minister Chi Haotian, came a day after the death of China's paramount leader, Deng Xiaoping.
The three ships will visit Pearl Harbor on March 9-13 and San Diego on March 21-25, defense officials said.

The Chinese naval training vessel Zheng He visited Pearl Harbor in April of 1989, but the upcoming visit would be the first to the U.S. mainland by Chinese warships, according to officials at the Navy's Pacific Command headquarters in Hawaii.

Despite differences over trade, human rights, Taiwan and arms proliferation, the United States and China have moved in recent months to improve relations. President Bill Clinton has stressed the importance of engaging the Asian giant rather than isolating it.
U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, currently on an 11-day, nine-country tour of Europe and Asia, her first overseas trip since taking office, is due in China next week.

Clinton said on Wednesday that he was saddened to hear of Deng's death, adding that Deng's 1979 visit to America had laid the foundation for a rapid expansion of relations and cooperation between the two countries.
